content.value_statement: Frontend layouts often break across mobile, tablet, and desktop sizes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to apply responsive components, breakpoints, and touch-friendly patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guides React component work in .tsx and .jsx files.
Applies mobile-first breakpoints for Tailwind CSS utilities.
Recommends CSS Grid and Flexbox layout patterns.
Encourages relative units for typography, spacing, and containers.
Covers touch-friendly buttons, tap targets, and gestures.
Supports review of mobile, tablet, and desktop behavior.
limitations: Does not include executable test scripts or visual regression tooling.
References an external standards file that should be packaged inside the skill.
Cannot verify device behavior without a browser or screenshot workflow.
Provides guidance only; implementation quality depends on the host project.

use_cases.title: Improve React Layouts
use_cases.description: Convert fixed component layouts into mobile-first structures with flexible spacing, wrapping, and breakpoint behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design System Components
use_cases.description: Review shared buttons, cards, grids, and navigation patterns for consistent responsive behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare Cross-Device Reviews
use_cases.description: Identify responsive risks before release across phone, tablet, and desktop screen widths.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Navigation Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my navigation for mobile menus, tablet spacing, desktop alignment, and touch target size.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Responsive Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a refactor plan for a multi-page frontend with grids, typography, spacing, and asset behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a product card for mobile and desktop behavior.
output: Identifies fixed widths that may overflow on small screens.
Suggests a stacked mobile layout with flexible media sizing.
Recommends breakpoint checks for text wrapping and action placement.

output_examples.input: Plan responsive navigation for a marketing site.
output: Defines mobile menu behavior and desktop navigation alignment.
Calls out minimum tap target size for primary actions.
Lists breakpoint checks for logo, links, and call-to-action buttons.

output_examples.input: Improve a dashboard grid for tablet screens.
output: Recommends flexible grid columns that collapse predictably.
Highlights card content that needs wrapping or reordering.
Adds review steps for spacing, charts, and dense controls.

best_practices: Start with mobile layout, then add larger breakpoint refinements.
Use relative units for spacing, type, and containers when practical.
Test core screens at phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
anti_patterns: Using fixed pixel widths for primary page containers.
Hiding essential actions on mobile without an alternate path.
Adding breakpoints without checking touch targets and content wrapping.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps AI coding tools build frontend layouts that adapt across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

faq.question: Does it support React projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill specifically mentions React component work in .tsx and .jsx files.

faq.question: Does it include Tailwind guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers responsive Tailwind utility breakpoints such as sm, md, lg, xl, and 2xl.

faq.question: Can it test responsive behavior automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but browser testing or screenshots must come from the host workflow.

faq.question: Is the skill limited to mobile screens?
faq.answer: No. It covers mobile-first design plus tablet and desktop refinements.

faq.question: What security concern was found?
faq.answer: The skill links to a parent-directory file outside the package. That referenced guidance should be included inside the reviewed skill.
